the photolysis of condensed-phase nitromethane and D3-nitro-methane at 5 K yields a variety of carbon-, oxygen-, nitrogen-centered radicals as well as atomic H, and that the carbon-centered nitro-methyl radical is a key intermediate for the formation of complex organic molecules.

the photolysis of solid nitromethane leads to the formation of carbon-centered methyl and nitromethyl radicals, as well as oxygen-centered methoxy radicals and nitrogen-centered nitrogen monoxide and dioxide radicals, which are the key intermediates leading to the formation of complex organic molecules via molecular mass growth.

the photolysis of solid nitromethane and D3-nitro-methane at 5 K leads to the formation of a multitude of carbon- and oxygen-centered radicals and atomic hydrogen (H), which are the precursors for a variety of molecular mass growth processes.

the elucidation of nonequilibrium reaction pathways in the photodecomposition of energetic materials in solid phase at 5K.
the elucidation of the chemical pathways in the photodecomposition of nitromethanes in a condensed phase environment.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photolysis of nitromethanes in the solid state at low temperatures is a very complex process, which is governed by the competition of several different reaction channels.

the decomposition of solid nitromethane and D3-nitro-methane at low temperatures is dominated by the photolysis of the nitromethylene moiety (CH2NO) and that the photodecomposition proceeds via the following sequence of reactions: CH2NO2 → NO + CH2O → NO2 + CH2 → NO + H + CH → CH2 + H → CH3 + H → CH4 + H.

the decomposition pathways of solid nitromethane and D3-nitramethane are similar in the low-energy regime (4.7-6.4 eV) and differ in the high-energy regime (6.4-10.2 e V) due to the formation of the nitromethane radical in the latter.

the photolytic decomposition of nitromethanes in the condensed phase is a complex process involving multiple reaction pathways and a variety of reaction intermediates and decomposition products.

the decomposition of nitromethanes in the solid phase proceeds via nonequilibrium reaction pathways, which are not accessible in the gas phase.
